cards.explanation: The answer is that He reveals Himself to them. The LORD says, “I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me.” (Isaiah 65:1) They weren't asking and they weren't seeking, and He still revealed Himself. He says, “Here I am! Here I am!” to a nation that did not call His name.

The answer is their own imaginations. The LORD says they walk in the wrong path and “…follow their own imaginations…” (Isaiah 65:2). Picture me baking from a recipe I made up at two in the morning. I'd feel REAL sure of myself right up until the oven opened.

The answer is in the gardens, friends. The LORD says they are “…sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense on altars of brick…” (Isaiah 65:3). Gardens and brick altars are the places He names. That's the answer here.

The answer is smoke in His nostrils, friends. “Such people are smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.” (Isaiah 65:5) They say, “Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you!” The LORD says that's what such people are to Him.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says they are “…smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.” (Isaiah 65:5) You get both in one line, the smoke and the fire. The fire is the part that burns all day long.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will pay it back into their laps…” (Isaiah 65:6) His people had asked whether He would keep silent (Isaiah 64:12). Here He speaks.

The answer is that they burned incense and scorned Him, friends. The LORD says, “Because they burned incense on the mountains and scorned Me on the hills, I will measure into their laps full payment for their former deeds.” (Isaiah 65:7) The mountains and hills are where He says it happened. He also says this repayment is for their iniquities and for those of their fathers.

The answer is that it contains a blessing, friends. In the LORD's picture, men say, “Do not destroy it, for it contains a blessing…” (Isaiah 65:8). Then the LORD says, “so I will act on behalf of My servants; I will not destroy them all.” (Isaiah 65:8)

The answer is True. The LORD says, “My elect will possess My mountains, and My servants will dwell there.” (Isaiah 65:9) He also promises descendants from Jacob and heirs from Judah in the same verse. They get a place to live, friends.

The answer is seek. Sharon becomes a pasture for flocks and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds, “…for My people who seek Me.” (Isaiah 65:10) Seeking is the word here. Verse 1 spoke of people who did not seek Him and were found anyway, and verse 10 speaks of His people who seek Him.

The answer is Fortune. The LORD says they “…set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny…” (Isaiah 65:11) Fortune gets a table while His holy mountain gets forgotten. I'd lay out a nice spread for a plate of cookies before I'd do that for luck.

The answer is that He called and they did not answer. The LORD says, “…I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen; you did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.” (Isaiah 65:12) He called and spoke, and they didn't answer or listen. Friends, that's a lot of knocking on a door.
The answer is False. The Lord GOD says, “My servants will eat, but you will go hungry…” (Isaiah 65:13) The servants eat and the others go hungry. He puts the two side by side on purpose.

The answer is that they will be put to shame, friends. The Lord GOD says, “My servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 65:13) One side rejoices and the other side is put to shame. The same verse says His servants will eat while the others go hungry, and drink while the others go thirsty. No middle ground in that verse.

The answer is True. The Lord GOD says, “but to His servants He will give another name.” (Isaiah 65:15) The others leave their name behind as a curse for His chosen ones, and His servants get a new one. Me, I got a name carved in my handle, and that was plenty.

The answer is forgotten, friends. “For the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from My sight.” (Isaiah 65:16) Forgotten is exactly what the LORD says about them. The verse also says the troubles are hidden from His sight.
